The total reflects the overall chip shortage in 2021, not the loss attributable to one fire. VEHICLES NOT BUILT 7.7M AlixPartners, Sep 2021 AUTOMOTIVE MCU SHARE ~30% Reuters, Mar 2021; Renesas
checks.notes: SLIDE 02 · 35 SECONDS · 0:25–1:00 In March 2021, fire hit Renesas, a firm supplying about thirty percent of automotive microcontrollers. That concentration exposed how one upstream facility could affect many manufacturers. Separately, AlixPartners estimated the entire 2021 chip shortage cost automakers two hundred and ten billion dollars and seven point seven million vehicles. We are not attributing that whole loss to one fire. The lesson is that a small-looking upstream dependency can become a system-wide production problem. checks.editableText: SHOCKTWIN Problem ShockTwin SAP Impact 03 / 14 SAP HACKFEST 2026 · RV UNIVERSITY RESILIENT SUPPLY CHAINS McKinsey Supply Chain Risk Survey 2024 03 · VISIBILITY Most  firms  can't see  past  tier  1. Beyond-tier-one visibility is shrinking when upstream exposure matters most. VISIBILITY BEYOND TIER ONE McKinsey Supply Chain Risk Survey 2024
checks.notes: SLIDE 03 · 30 SECONDS · 1:00–1:30 Yet visibility is moving in the wrong direction. McKinsey's survey reports visibility beyond tier one falling from fifty-six percent in 2022, to thirty-seven percent, to thirty percent in 2024. This is not a forecast; it is the published survey series. If a purchasing dashboard stops at direct suppliers, it can display several alternatives while missing the single upstream dependency that makes them fail together. SOURCE / QUALIFICATION (not additional spoken copy): McKinsey Supply Chain Risk Survey 2024

checks.notes: SLIDE 04 · 30 SECONDS · 1:30–2:00 The iceberg is the problem. About two-thirds of disruptions originate at tier two or deeper, according to McKinsey. Only about ten percent of firms see their tier-three suppliers, and the average response to a new disruption is about two weeks. These measures come from different published observations, not one experiment. ShockTwin asks a practical question: can a buyer identify a consequential hidden dependency and act while inventory still gives them time? India  paid. Disrupted shipping routes transmitted cost pressure to Indian supply chains; the sea was not literally closed. SUEZ TRAFFIC -57% UNCTAD; from peak to Oct 2024 SHANGHAI–EUROPE SPOT +256% UNCTAD, 2024 INDIA–EUROPE CONTAINER COST $600 $1,500 Reuters, Jan 2024 · approximate costs
checks.notes: SLIDE 05 · 30 SECONDS · 2:00–2:30 The Red Sea illustrates how a distant route becomes a local cost. The sea was disrupted, not literally closed. UNCTAD reports Suez traffic down fifty-seven percent from its peak by October 2024 and Shanghai–Europe spot rates up two hundred and fifty-six percent. Reuters reported India–Europe container costs moving from about six hundred to fifteen hundred dollars in January. Different periods, different measures, one message: geography does not contain supply-chain consequences. SOURCE / QUALIFICATION (not additional spoken copy): Reuters, Jan 2024 · UNCTAD, 2024 · Different measures and periods

checks.editableText: SHOCKTWIN Problem ShockTwin SAP Impact 06 / 14 SAP HACKFEST 2026 · RV UNIVERSITY RESILIENT SUPPLY CHAINS Bloomberg, Apr 2021 · Fortune, Jan 2022 06 · THE COUNTEREXAMPLE Toyota  survived because  it had  a  map. Mapping upstream dependencies can turn a hidden concentration into a decision. CRITICAL PARTS MAPPED ~1,500 Bloomberg Apr 2021 / Fortune Jan 2022 US OUTPUT KEPT ~90% Bloomberg Apr 2021 / Fortune Jan 2022 GM UNITS CUT ~278,000 Bloomberg Apr 2021 / Fortune Jan 2022
checks.notes: SLIDE 06 · 30 SECONDS · 2:30–3:00 There is a useful counterexample. After 2011, Toyota mapped about fifteen hundred critical parts. During the chip crisis it kept US production near ninety percent, while GM cut about two hundred and seventy-eight thousand units. The cited reporting does not prove that mapping alone caused that difference. It shows why upstream knowledge deserves attention. Our aim is to make mapping actionable through a connected warning, rehearsal and response workflow. SOURCE / QUALIFICATION (not additional spoken copy): Bloomberg, Apr 2021 · Fortune, Jan 2022

checks.notes: SLIDE 08 · 40 SECONDS · 3:20–4:00 Meet Priya, our illustrative procurement head at a Bengaluru auto-parts manufacturer. She starts with five immediate suppliers. We run the model and reveal a candidate shared resin plant behind three of them. The dashed edges carry actual synthetic-model scores and evidence; they are hypotheses, not verified commercial relationships. Priya can confirm or reject them. Our GraphSAGE model is trained on synthetic data; its measured test results are labelled accordingly. The research basis is supplier-network link prediction by Kosasih and Brintrup, not a borrowed accuracy claim. Illustrative: a day-three replacement switch avoids a line stop through the displayed simulation horizon. SIMULATE · REAL APP · ILLUSTRATIVE Illustrative local app · actual browser capture RESIN STOCK LEFT · ILLUSTRATIVE 0 6 12 18 24 30 DAY 18 DAY-3 SWITCH DAY 18 · STOCK-OUT Real local API · 100 units/day · 30-day horizon
checks.notes: SLIDE 09 · 45 SECONDS · 4:00–4:45 Now we rehearse the cyclone. This is the real simulator, using illustrative inputs: eighteen hundred resin units and demand of one hundred units per day. Under the default full-loss shock, baseline stock reaches zero on day eighteen. Switch on replacement flow after day three, and the curve holds at fifteen hundred units because replacement covers daily demand. That avoids a line stop through this displayed horizon. It is conditional on timing, volume and availability, not a promise of endless continuity. We can change severity, duration and switch timing to see where the plan fails. SOURCE / QUALIFICATION (not additional spoken copy): Illustrative local simulation · Assumptions and real app result in screenshot

checks.notes: SLIDE 10 · 45 SECONDS · 4:45–5:30 CapacityMesh is the response step. We request suitable moulding capacity, inspect the eligible matches and see exactly how capability, distance, volume, lead time and price band affect ranking. Only minimal capacity envelopes are public; raw transactions stay private. Priya drafts a purchase order, reviews it in the inbox and approves it, leaving an audit trail. The local ERP is explicitly a mock. India's empty-running and utilisation figures suggest capacity worth investigating, while the ventilator collaboration shows precedent. They do not prove every idle asset is usable, and our minutes headline describes the demonstrated workflow, not physical production activation. checks.notes: SLIDE 11 · 35 SECONDS · 5:30–6:05 The target platform is SAP BTP. SAPUI5 provides the Horizon interface; CAP owns the domain services; HANA Cloud holds graph, vector and relational data; AI Core and AI Launchpad host the model; and Generative AI Hub supports bounded explanations. Integration Suite connects enterprise and external sources, while Build Process Automation routes approval. Today the complete local flow runs with SQLite and explicit mocks. Live SAP service bindings and purchasing semantics still require verification. Human authorization remains the final control. SOURCE / QUALIFICATION (not additional spoken copy): SAP target architecture: project design · Live cloud integration [VERIFY]
